provenance.resolutionNote: Saving a quote draft is an internal product operation, not a legal act — same reasoning as fr.json/us.json for this same action: no text identified that would specifically govern this act under Italian law. To be revisited if the product were one day to give legal effect to the mere fact of saving a draft.

provenance.sourceText: An electronic signature shall not be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for qualified electronic signatures.

rules.notes: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS), Art. 25 § 1 — the SAME citation, read live on 2026-09-03 on eur-lex.europa.eu, as de.json/pl.json/es.json's own quote.send: a European regulation applies directly, with no national transposition, so it is identical for Italy. A quote is not an invoice (see invoice.send below, specific to Italian tax law): it is this general regime of non-discrimination against the electronic written form that grounds the sending of a quote.

provenance.resolutionNote: Converting an accepted quote into an invoice is a product convenience; no text identified imposes or prohibits this precise mechanism under Italian law (the only legal constraint would bear on the resulting invoice). To be confirmed by a dedicated review should a specific traceability rule ever come to attach to it.

Requesting a deposit on a quote, in the form of a draft deposit invoice, is a product convenience of the same nature as 'convert-to-invoice' above; no text identified governs this precise mechanism under Italian law. To be confirmed by a dedicated review should a specific rule come to attach to the deposit request itself.

Generating a billing schedule from an accepted quote (several draft invoices, one per installment) is a product convenience of the same nature as 'request-deposit' above; no text identified governs this precise mechanism under Italian law (the only legal constraint would bear on the resulting invoices once issued, not on the creation of these drafts). To be confirmed by a dedicated review should a specific rule come to attach to the generation of a schedule itself.

Duplicating a quote into a new draft is a pure product convenience; no text identified governs it under Italian law. To be confirmed by a dedicated review before extending this mechanism to a document type whose duplication would carry a legal stake.

Generating a public, unauthenticated link to a quote's PDF is a product convenience — a quote is not even a tax document. No text identified that would specifically govern the sharing of a link to a document already communicated to its recipient; the link itself remains subject to the token security discipline (share-links/share-links.service.ts). To be confirmed by a dedicated review if applicable.

Asking a customer to electronically sign a quote (link + OTP code by email — signatures/signatures.service.ts) is a product convenience — signing a quote is not a legally governed act, it is a mark of commercial acceptance. The mechanism stays at the lowest eIDAS level (SIMPLE electronic signature), never a certificate, so no Italian text on advanced/qualified electronic signatures applies here. To be confirmed by a dedicated review if applicable.

NO legal research was performed for this entry - unlike this rule's neighbors above, this note does not claim any text was read. Allowed because this action records an ISSUER-SIDE FACT ONLY - who marked a sent quote accepted, when, and by what means - and changes no fiscal fact and produces no document a third party ever receives, the same kind of internal record quote.duplicate above already sits on. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS: a text conditioning the evidentiary value, or the validity, of a quote's acceptance on the channel through which it was obtained - to be confirmed by a dedicated review before this record is relied on as a substitute for a legally regulated acceptance mechanism.

provenance.sourceText: Inexistant : aucun instrument d'amendement par référence — le provvedimento ne cadre les variations que comme note di credito ou di debito ex art. 26.

rules.notes: REUSES the citation already read by correction-routes/data/it.json (route CORRECTIVE_INVOICE, forbidden) — Provv. AdE 89757/2018, punto 6.1, checked on 2026-08-29 (date preserved as-is: reused, not re-verified by this task). This is the CLEAREST citation among the five new countries on this precise fact: Italy EXPLICITLY prohibits any correction-by-reference mechanism on a document already transmitted to the Sistema di Interscambio (SdI) — an Italian invoice accepted by the SdI can ONLY be corrected by a nota di credito or di debito (separate documents, art. 26 DPR 633/72), never by re-saving a draft on the same document. The `statuses: ["draft"]` field applies this principle by refusing to re-save as draft an invoice already 'sent' — same mechanics as fr.json/de.json above, each sourced to its own national text for the SAME fact: the immutability of the ISSUED invoice (in the Italian sense: accepted by the SdI).

provenance.sourceText: Per fattura elettronica si intende la fattura che è stata emessa e ricevuta in un qualunque formato elettronico. [...] il ricorso alla fattura elettronica è subordinato all'accettazione da parte del destinatario.

rules.notes: Art. 21, comma 1, DPR 633/1972. Read live on 2026-09-03 on normattiva.it (the official portal of the Italian Republic for consolidated texts in force — the Italian equivalent of Légifrance/gesetze-im-internet.de/BOE). This text explicitly recognizes the validity of the Italian ELECTRONIC invoice, the equivalent of VI of art. 289 CGI (French) or § 14 Abs. 1 UStG (German). NUANCE NOT MODELED HERE (same limitation as fr.json/de.json's own invoice.send): the text conditions recourse to the electronic invoice on THE RECIPIENT'S ACCEPTANCE — except that, unlike France or Germany, Italy has made transmission via the Sistema di Interscambio (SdI) MANDATORY for nearly all domestic invoicing since 2019 (fact already flagged, but left 'unverified'/'suggested' for lack of a citation of its own, dated to its own consultation date, in transports/channel-policy/data/it.json — a DISTINCT subject, the channel/mandate, outside the scope of this rule which only covers the admissibility of the electronic SENDING itself).

provenance.resolutionNote: Duplicating an invoice into a new draft is the same pure product convenience as quote.duplicate above — the new document is born 'draft' and re-enters the normal issuance circuit in full, so no text identified governs the act of duplication itself under Italian law. The tax question (DPR 633/72) bears on the ISSUED INVOICE that will result from it, not on this initial draft. To be confirmed by a dedicated review should a specific rule ever come to attach to the automated creation of invoice drafts.

Recording a payment is an internal accounting entry; no specific text identified that would govern the mere fact of declaring it in this tool. The resulting balance is a PROJECTION displayed on screen, never a status of the document — see invoice.descriptor.ts.

EN 16931 is a European TECHNICAL STANDARD (directive 2014/55/EU) — it is not in itself an Italian legal obligation for THIS company to produce it. The national format actually mandated in Italy is FatturaPA, transmitted via the SdI (a DISTINCT subject, the imposed channel/format — see transports/channel-policy/data/it.json, left 'suggested'/unverified for lack of a citation of its own, dated to its own consultation date), outside the scope of this rule which only builds the voluntary standardized EN 16931 FORMAT, the same distinction as fr.json/de.json/us.json for the same action. This rule therefore authorizes the voluntary DOWNLOAD of an EN 16931 export without asserting that it is legally required IN THIS PRECISE FORM.

Exporting an invoice to an accounting tool is a product convenience; no specific text identified that would govern the mere fact of offering this export. This action has in any case no registered implementation to date (see invoice-actions.ts) — the actual block comes from the 501, not from this rule.

Generating a public, unauthenticated link to an invoice's PDF is a product convenience of the same order as 'download-xml' just above: no text identified specifically imposes or prohibits the sharing of a link to an invoice already communicated to its legitimate recipient. The link's security is a technical guarantee documented in share-links/share-links.service.ts, not a distinct legal requirement to source here.

Saving a credit note draft is an internal product operation. The legal regime of the Italian nota di credito (see credit-note.send below) concerns the CONTENT and the tax status of the document, not the act of saving a draft — same distinction as fr.json/de.json for this same action.

provenance.sourceText: ha diritto di portare in detrazione [...] ; commas 9 et 10 qualifient cette voie de « facoltà » — nature : faculté, jamais obligation.

rules.notes: REUSES the citation already read by correction-routes/data/it.json (route CREDIT_NOTE, allowed) — Art. 26 DPR 633/72, comma 2, checked on 2026-08-29 (date preserved: reused, not re-verified by this task). The precise fact this SEND needs — is issuing a document that reduces the amount of an Italian invoice (the nota di credito, document type TD04 in the SdI nomenclature) legally open — is exactly what this citation settles: it is a FACULTY (option) opened by art. 26 comma 2 DPR 633/72, never an obligation (unlike the increase case — DEBIT_NOTE, comma 1, 'DEVONO ESSERE OSSERVATE' — the canonical Italian asymmetry, not relevant for this decrease SEND). Distinct from fr.json/de.json's own choice to leave credit-note.send unverified: here a clear citation, specific to the DECREASE direction, already exists in this repo (correction-routes) and settles exactly this fact, so it is promoted.

provenance.resolutionNote: Same reasoning as invoice.share-link above, applied to the credit note: no text identified specifically governs the sharing of a public link to a credit note already communicated to its recipient.

Issue #472. The FORMAT fact is read first-hand, not the statute: the Agenzia delle Entrate FatturaPA schema this repository vendors and validates every FatturaPA file against (formats/vendored/it/Schema_VFPR12.xsd, version 1.2) enumerates `TipoDocumento` value TD04 with the documentation « Nota di credito », and declares `DatiFattureCollegate` (type DatiDocumentiCorrelatiType: IdDocumento, Data) as the slot for the invoices a document relates to - read 2026-09-27. The provider builds TD04 with that block naming the corrected invoice, and the file passes the XSD (formats/credit-note-formats.spec.ts). The statutory basis of the nota di credito is art. 26, comma 2, DPR 633/72, already cited by this file's own credit-note.send rule (reused, not re-read here). What would make this `legal`: the Provvedimento del Direttore dell'Agenzia delle Entrate n. 89757 del 30 aprile 2018, Allegato A (Specifiche tecniche), read first-hand for TD04 and for whether DatiFattureCollegate is mandatory on a TD04 - not read in this session.

rules.notes: FatturaPA's `Numero` is at most 20 characters (String20Type). The old shared credit-note default "CREDIT-NOTE-2026-0001" was 21, so a TD04 could not be produced with default settings. Since issue #496 the Italian credit-note format comes from this file's own `numberFormats` ("CN-{year}-{number:4}", checked against it-fatturapa-numero-string20 at load time), and the XSD gate still refuses a longer number rather than truncate it (formats/credit-note-formats.spec.ts).

provenance.resolutionNote: Recording an expense is an internal management entry within the tool. Italian accounting obligations bear on the company's own bookkeeping, not on this recording mechanism within the tool. To be confirmed by a dedicated review should this core ever come to produce enforceable accounting documents from this data.

Deleting an incorrectly entered expense; no text identified specifically governs the deletion of such an entry before any accounting closing. To be confirmed by a dedicated review should this core ever come to distinguish a "closed" state for an expense.

Recording (or correcting) the fields of a received invoice is an internal management operation — this tool only records a fact that has already occurred, never issues anything. The `statuses` field restricts the rewriting of fields to the 'received' status alone: once approved or rejected, the review decision must no longer be silently undone (same mechanics as `invoice.save-draft` above). Not researched here: Italy receives its domestic invoices via the SdI, an accredited channel (a distinct subject, outside the scope of this internal approval workflow).
Marking a received invoice as approved is an internal company review decision; no text identified specifically governs this act.
Marking a received invoice as rejected (dispute, supplier error) is an internal company review decision; no text identified specifically governs this act.

Recording that this company paid a supplier is an internal bookkeeping entry, the mirror of `invoice.record-payment` above but on the buyer side of a purchase — no text identified specifically governs the ACT of recording it in this tool (as opposed to the underlying payment/input-VAT-deduction facts, which exist and produce their own legal effects regardless of whether this screen tracks them). Not independently researched for Italy beyond the reasoning already applied to `received-invoice.approve`/`reject` above (2026-09-16).

Deleting a received-invoice record before any approval/rejection decision is a product convenience, of the same nature as `expense.delete` above; no text identified governs it. The descriptor already restricts this action to the 'received' status alone.

Saving a purchase order draft is an internal product operation, unrelated to VAT or invoicing — same reasoning as quote.save-draft above (see its own note for the research conducted on the applicable codes): no text identified that would specifically govern the saving of such a draft. A purchase order also commits less than a quote (it does not constitute a sales offer, only a purchase intent of the issuing company itself), which makes the existence of a text targeting it all the less likely. Research not specifically conducted for this type/action (2026-09-15) — to be revisited should a real need require it.

provenance.sourceText: An electronic signature shall not be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for qualified electronic signatures.

rules.notes: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS), Art. 25 § 1 — the SAME text, at the same verification date, as quote.send above (see its own note: a European REGULATION applies directly, with no national variant, in every Member State). A purchase order is neither an invoice nor a quote, but an electronic document like any other with regard to this text: it is this same general regime of non-discrimination against the electronic written form that grounds its sending by email, never a text specific to invoicing or VAT (none exists for this type — see purchase-order.descriptor.ts's own header).

provenance.resolutionNote: Canceling a purchase order sent to a supplier is a purely commercial act (the company renounces its own order), never the correction of a tax document already transmitted — it is NOT a correction route within the meaning of correction-routes/ (CANCEL_AND_REPLACE and the other routes of that module only concern a tax document ALREADY ISSUED to a third party whose correction is governed by law, which a purchase order is not — see purchase-order-actions.ts's own header). The contractual consequences of such a cancellation toward the supplier fall under ordinary contract law, outside the scope of this rule (which only states whether THIS TOOL can record the entry, never whether the cancellation is enforceable against the supplier). No dedicated research conducted for this type/action (2026-09-15) — to be revisited should a real need require it.

Saving a goods-receipt draft is an internal, purely documentary operation (what this company's warehouse has recorded as received) — same reasoning as purchase-order.save-draft above: no text identified that would specifically govern the saving of such a draft, this document not being transmitted to anyone (see goods-receipt.descriptor.ts's own header). Research not specifically conducted for this type/action, newly created (2026-09-15) — to be revisited should a real need require it.

Finalizing a goods receipt (status 'recorded') is an internal management act — closing out what the warehouse has recorded as received against a purchase order, to feed a 3-way matching check that is itself internal to the tool, never transmitted to a third party nor declared to an administration. No text identified that would specifically target this act. Research not specifically conducted for this type/action, newly created (2026-09-15) — to be revisited should a real need require it.

Restricted by the descriptor itself to the 'draft' status (goods-receipt.descriptor.ts): once recorded ('recorded'), a goods receipt is part of the matching trail that a received invoice may already have been compared against, and its deletion is in any case no longer offered by the screen. Before that, deleting an incorrectly entered draft is the same internal operation, with no recipient, as purchase-order.save-draft/received-invoice.delete above (see their own notes for the tension, not settled here either, on the retention obligations for a supporting document — LPF art. L. 102 B and L. 102 C, C. com. art. L. 123-22 — which target the RECEIVED INVOICE, never a goods receipt by name). Research not specifically conducted for this type/action, newly created (2026-09-15) — to be revisited should a real need require it.

notes: Italy - research from 2026-09-03. The acts internal to the product follow the same reasoning already held by fr.json/us.json for the same actions. The legal weight rests on two sources: (1) a FRESH, DIRECT reading from 2026-09-03 on normattiva.it (the official Italian portal for consolidated texts) for art. 21 comma 1 DPR 633/1972 (invoice.send) and on eur-lex.europa.eu for the eIDAS regulation (quote.send); (2) the REUSE, dated and not re-verified, of citations already read on 2026-08-29 by correction-routes/data/it.json for the immutability of the issued invoice (invoice.save-draft, CORRECTIVE_INVOICE forbidden - the clearest citation among the five new countries on this fact) and for the credit note (credit-note.send, CREDIT_NOTE allowed) - each one only holds for the exact fact it settles here, never stretched beyond that.

provenance.resolutionNote: art. 21, comma 2, lett. b) DPR 633/1972 requires the invoice to carry « un numero progressivo che la identifichi in modo univoco » (read verbatim as quoted by Agenzia delle Entrate, Risposta n. 505 del 29 ottobre 2020, PDF on agenziaentrate.gov.it, 2026-09-26). No sentence was read that extends art. 21 to the nota di credito of art. 26, comma 2 (art. 26, comma 1 applies art. 21 only to the upward variation - see correction-routes/data/it.json's own DEBIT_NOTE fact). The SdI data model gives every document type, TD04 nota di credito included, a field 2.1.1.4 <Numero>. What would settle it: Circolare 20/E del 29/12/2021 (on art. 26) or the SdI technical specifications, read first-hand, for TD04.

numbering.notes: Product numbers Italian credit notes anyway - the SdI data model's own mandatory <Numero> field for TD04 is a strong practical signal even without a statutory sentence extending art. 21 to it, pending the first-hand read that would turn this into a `legal` entry.

constraints.summary: Italian law requires a progressive number that identifies the invoice uniquely. It constrains no character and no length.

provenance.resolutionNote: art. 21, comma 2, lett. b) DPR 633/1972 requires the invoice to carry « un numero progressivo che la identifichi in modo univoco » - quoted as this file's credit-note `numbering` fact read it on 2026-09-26 (via Agenzia delle Entrate, Risposta n. 505 del 29 ottobre 2020), NOT re-read first-hand in this pass. Found on 2026-09-28: normattiva.it now marks art. 21 as abrogated by D.Lgs. 19 gennaio 2026, n. 10 (Testo unico IVA), whose provisions apply from 1 January 2027 according to secondary sources (FiscoeTasse, FiscoOggi); its invoicing chapter (Capo V, arts. 72-96) could not be read (normattiva served only the table of contents). What would settle it: the Testo unico IVA's invoice-content article read first-hand, to confirm the « numero progressivo » requirement carries over unchanged from 2027.

constraints.summary: FatturaPA's <Numero> (2.1.1.4) holds at most 20 Basic Latin characters, for an invoice (TD01) and a credit note (TD04) alike. A longer number makes the file invalid, and the SdI rejects it.
constraints.notes: The Agenzia delle Entrate schema this repository vendors and validates every FatturaPA file against (formats/vendored/it/Schema_VFPR12.xsd, version 1.2), read on 2026-09-28. `allowedCharacters` is printable Basic Latin (space to tilde): a normalizedString admits no tab or line break, and Basic Latin's control characters have no place in a number.

constraints.summary: The SdI rejects a FatturaPA whose <Numero> contains no digit (error 00425).

provenance.sourceText: Codice 00425   2.1.1.4 <Numero> non contenente caratteri numerici [...] IF ( Numero non contiene ValoreNum ) E R R O R E (00425)

constraints.notes: « Elenco dei controlli effettuati sul file fattura del Sistema di Interscambio », versione 1.9, https://www.fatturapa.gov.it/export/documenti/Elenco-Controlli-versione-1.9.pdf, read first-hand with pdftotext on 2026-09-28. Every shipped format carries a {number} token, so it always holds; stated so a running series is judged against it too.

resetProvenance.sourceText: Conseguentemente, a decorrere dal 1° gennaio 2013, può essere adottata una numerazione progressiva che, partendo dal numero 1, prosegua ininterrottamente per tutti gli anni solari di attività del contribuente, fino alla cessazione dell'attività stessa. [...] Peraltro, qualora risulti più agevole, il contribuente può continuare ad adottare il sistema di numerazione progressiva per anno solare, in quanto l'identificazione univoca della fattura è, anche in tal caso, comunque garantita dalla contestuale presenza nel documento della data che, in base alla lettera a) del citato articolo 21, costituisce un elemento obbligatorio della fattura. Ad esempio, [...] si ritengono ammissibili le seguenti modalità di numerazione progressiva all'interno di ciascun anno solare: [...] Fatt. n. 1/2013 (oppure n. 2013/1) [...]

formats.notes: Agenzia delle Entrate, Risoluzione n. 1/E del 10 gennaio 2013, "Chiarimenti in materia di numerazione delle fatture" (art. 21, comma 2, lett. b, DPR 633/1972) - official PDF https://www.agenziaentrate.gov.it/portale/documents/20143/304338/Risoluzione+1++10012013a_risoluzione+1e.pdf, downloaded and read first-hand with pdftotext on 2026-09-28. Explicit, on-point administrative confirmation that a calendar-year progressive series (e.g. "1/2013", exactly this product's {number}/{year} or {year}-{number} shape) remains lawful after the 2013 reform, since the invoice's own mandatory date (art. 21 comma 2 lett. a) already disambiguates a number that repeats across years - the same "the pair (date, number) is enough" principle this file's own fr-cgi-242-nonies-a analogue rests on in fr.json. STILL GOOD PAST THE 2027 CUTOVER: the successor Testo unico IVA (D.Lgs. 19 gennaio 2026, n. 10), read first-hand from the official Gazzetta Ufficiale PDF (Suppl. ord. n. 4/L alla G.U. n. 24 del 30-1-2026) on 2026-09-28, carries the identical requirement verbatim at art. 72, comma 2, lett. b) ("numero progressivo che la identifichi in modo univoco", the article heading itself printing "(articolo 21 decreto del Presidente della Repubblica 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633)" as its source) and art. 171 ("Decorrenza": "Le disposizioni del presente testo unico si applicano a decorrere dal 1° gennaio 2027") carries no transitional clause narrowing or reopening the numbering question. A straight recodification of the identical wording Risoluzione 1/E interpreted, so its conclusion is read as continuing to govern unchanged.

formats.rationale: The product's previous shared default, "CREDIT-NOTE-{year}-{number:4}", renders 21 characters ("CREDIT-NOTE-2026-0001"), over the 20 that Chorus Pro (B2G) and FatturaPA accept. "CN-" keeps the credit note at 14 characters at number 999999, in a series of its own, distinct from the invoice series. With it, an Italian credit note produces a valid TD04 with default settings (issue #496).

resetProvenance.resolutionNote: Risoluzione n. 1/E/2013 (this file's own invoice `resetProvenance`, read first-hand 2026-09-28) addresses only the fattura under art. 21/art. 72 - never the nota di credito. This file's own credit-note `numbering` fact already leaves UNVERIFIED whether a credit note needs a progressive number under Italian law at all (no sentence read extends art. 21/art. 26, now art. 72/art. 92, to it), and it-dpr-633-art-21 is deliberately NOT bound to the credit-note format for the same reason (constrainedBy above lists only the FatturaPA/SdI technical constraints, never it-dpr-633-art-21). Extending the invoice's yearly-reset permission to a document whose own numbering requirement is itself unsettled would overclaim; stays the safe default until a source addresses the credit note directly.

Found on 2026-09-28: normattiva.it now marks art. 21 as abrogated by D.Lgs. 19 gennaio 2026, n. 10 (Testo unico IVA), whose provisions apply from 1 January 2027 according to secondary sources (FiscoeTasse, FiscoOggi); its invoicing chapter (Capo V, arts. 72-96) could not be read (normattiva served only the table of contents). runningSeries.onViolation: If the running series breaks a FatturaPA rule above (for example a number over 20 characters, such as the old default "CREDIT-NOTE-2026-0001"), the country format applies from the next number. The counter is not reset, so the number stays progressive and unique; only the printed prefix changes. Such a series could not have produced a valid FatturaPA file anyway.
